instruments.title: Drum with a tapered hollow tree-trunk body, cow hide skin and enclosed base, as well as attached twisted sinew strands, cloth and leather strap. Recorded in related documentation as a Chief's drum or possible Royal drum, 'Mujaguzo'. Signs of damage.

A wooden drum with a rounded head covered in skin, fixed with wooden pegs, a long cylindrical body and a flared foot. A length of cotton cloth is attached through drilled holes on the side of the head and foot.
Wooden drum on three cylindrical legs with irregularly shaped skin glued to the body. A length of rope is wrapped around the legs.

Large hide trumpet; wide at one end, narrow at other. Gourd attachment fits into wider end of trumpet; a ring of long black hair attached to gourd. Circular blowhole present near narrow end. Pest activity in present in hair; white accretions on hide; gourd broken.

Wooden trumpet with cylinder of gourd at wide end, entirely covered in hide. The section of hide around the oval mouthpiece and finger stop retains the hair. There is a loop of sinew cord attached between the two openings.
Iron cow bell. Cylinder, open at both sides, with long cylindrical iron clapper attached to a ring at the top of the bell. Long twisted fibre cord also attached to ring.
Iron bell. Spherical bell with slit along the middle, containing an iron ball, damaged hole on one side. Skin/hide strap threaded through two holes at the reverse of the bell. Used as a dog bell.

Iron bell, crescent shaped with slit along one edge and two holes along the other edge. Inside is an iron ball. Threaded through the holes is a strap of leather. Worn by boy or young people especially for dances.

Jjembe. Power object made from a horse tail with an iron bell suspended from the end. The tail is attached to a bulbous shaped object that is bound in hide with some hair remaining, it is suspended from a length of twisted leather. At the base is a wrapped string of beads that are blue, white and red in colour. Used as a protection against missiles.

household.title: Woven bird cage or basket. Roughly cylindrical in shape, with a circular handle attached to top and rounded base; fibre rope tied around handle. Pest damage present.
Lyre with a bowl shaped resonator covered in crocodile skin, a broadly triangular wooden frame with two hair terminals, and eight sinew or fibre twisted strings. There is evidence of damage.
Horn with oval blowhole close to the point and circular finger stop. Cylindrical section of gourd around wide end.
Nakalondo. Bottle-shaped jjembe or power object, likely made of wood, covered with skin that has been stitched down both sides.  A strip of plantain leaf string is tied around the top.

Jjembe. Power object. Pear-shaped container covered in hide, around the neck are three copper alloy rings and one iron ring with lengths of hide and fibre tied to it. The opening at the top of the neck is wooden.

ceramic.title: A globular beer pot with two short necked openings at the top. Each opening is circular with an everted rim and is decorated below the neck with textured diagonal lines. The base is rounded and is decorated at the centre with textured lines that form a loose spiral.

arms.title: Knife. Short iron blade, flat, curved at the tip. Wooden handle, cylindrical grip that widens to an oval at the base of the blade.

Spear, with split-socketed iron spearhead. Long, leaf-shaped blade with central midrib. Long, split-socketed ferrule with a rectangular, tapering end. The wooden shaft is girded by two metal bands. Spearhead and ferrule are secured with metal rivets.
Spear, with split-socketed iron spearhead. Leaf-shaped blade with central midrib and long shank. Wooden shaft.

Wooden shield, covered with strips of plant fibre that are arranged horizontally across the front and back and held in place with vertical bands. The shield is round and convex; the shape is like a circle that has been folded vertically back on itself down the middle. There is a conical central boss with loop of twine threaded through it, and a border of raw hide with lots of long black hair still attached around the edge. The handle is a bundle of twigs, fastened lengthways inside the bend of the shield.

Chief's shield. Convex oval basketry shield of woven cane with a pigmented wooden umbo or central boss and a corresponding attached fibre loop, two single bands of woven triangles near the edge, as well as a vertical bound wooden handle upon the reverse. The shield is edged with hide and long straight dark hair.

Wooden shield, covered with strips of plant fibre that are arranged horizontally across the front and back and held in place with vertical bands. The shield is round and convex; the shape is like a circle that has been folded vertically back on itself down the middle. There is a central boss, and a border of hide attached around the edge with plant fibre stitches. The handle, made from twigs and fibre, is fastened lengthways inside the bend of the shield, and has a knotted loop of plant fibre rope threaded through.

Wooden shield, covered with strips of plant fibre that are arranged horizontally across the front and back and held in place with vertical bands. The shield is round and convex; the shape is like a circle that has been folded vertically back on itself down the middle. There is a central boss with a hide string threaded through it, and a border of raw hide with black hair still attached around the edge. The handle is a bundle of twigs, fastened lengthways inside the bend of the shield.

textile.title: A cloak made from barkcloth, that has been decorated with a black dyed geometric design. The top of the cloak has a looped opening, that likely fitted the cloak around the wearer's neck. This opening is adorned with a pointed horn-like piece, likely made from wood and covered in hide, that would point up from the wearer's shoulder at an angle of about 45º, and two pleated, triangular pieces of barkcloth that look like a large bow.

jewelry.title: Iron bracelet. Two twisted bands becoming one towards the ends, both ends curved into spirals. Worn by women.
Woman's brass bracelet. Heavy solid circle with circular cross-section.
An ivory ornament for upper arm of chief. An oval ring with a rectangular cross section. Dark brown patina on outer edge.
Woman's hollow iron anklet. It is round with an opening, and is circular in cross-section.

other.title: Lyre with lizard skin covered resonator and seven strings. [MJD 25/09/2008]

A lyre with two wooden arms and a crossbar from which strips of cotton and multiple strings, possibly sinew, are tied and connected to the sound box. The sound box is a carved wooden bowl, with reptile skin covering the top and a patch of hide on the bottom, connected to the skin with multiple strings. Strings broken and some repaired with nylon thread.

Tube bound with string, and filter for beer drinking. The tube itself is of hollow pliable wood, and is tightly bound with string. The filter at one end is an oval of thin strips of twig, interwoven cross-ways with fibre. The twigs comprising the filter are bound to the end of the tube with a spiral binding of flat bark.
Digging stick carved from a single piece of wood. Cylindrical handle flattening into a leaf-shaped blade with point; heartwood visible on one side.
Long twisted horn with oval mouth hole close to the point and small perforations around the wide end.

Animal horn with oval mouth hole and finger stop at tip; tip surrounded by hide. A length of plant fibre cord is threaded through a hole in the open end and is attached to a small iron bell by an iron loop.

Gomba; Mahamba. Power object (jjembe) made of wood; one terminal is bulbous and coated in hide, and the other is an iron spike. The body of the charm is wrapped in iron rings in two places, with another bulbous section just above the iron ferrule. This section, and below bulbous terminal the body of the charm is decorated with small, disc shaped ostrich egg-shells. Lower section is coated in clay with small blue beads pressed into the surface. The body is also bound in twine in places.

Jjembe. Power object covered in brown fibre. Ovoid in shape, it is bundled together at each end to form two cylindrical knobs. The contents of the bundle is unclear, but there is a small piece of metal protruding from one side. A piece of bark cord is tied to one end, and a piece of hide cord is tied to the other.

Bala Kuisali and Kisinda. Two leather pear-shaped mayembe or power objects. The kisinda [.1] is larger, and its leather cover is decorated with cowry shells. It has a perforation at the top through which a metal suspension loop is attached. The kuisali [.2] is smaller and is also covered in leather. There are perforations in the sides of both charms, which allow them to be tied to each other with a long loop of twisted fibre.

Gomba. Power object (jjembe) covered in brown leather. One terminal is rounded with four cylinders of wood attached to twisted cord; the body tapers towards the other terminal which is narrow and flat. The leather is stitched at either end.
Jjembe. Power object. Cylindrical, wider at one end and covered in hide. Attached to the wider end is a hide loop, and to the other end a plume of long dark hair.
